item.title: The Yen Carry Trade, a Piano and Trump’s World View
item.description: When the Bank of Japan raises its policy rate to 0.75%, that unsettles global finance, accustomed as the world is to borrowing ultra-cheap in yen and investing in assets denominated in other currencies, the yields in whose economies are significantly higher than in Japan.

item.title: Global Trade Shifts, AI Speculation and India’s Growth Prospects in 2026
item.description: As 2026 nears, AI hype meets revenue reality, tariffs fade, but India’s growth faces weak demand, rural stress and rising risks.

item.title: What’s wrong with the SHANTI Act and how it can be fixed
item.description: The government should have referred the Bill to a parliamentary committee to iron out differences, instead of using its legislative majority to pass it as introduced.

item.title: India and the 28th CSPOC: Parliamentary Democracy in a Fragmented Global Order
item.description: The Conference of Speakers and Presiding Officers of the Commonwealth has emerged as a unique institution that upholds parliamentary independence and is non-partisan, even as it derives much from the Westminster system and traditions, and underscores the neutrality and authority of speakers.

item.title: Urbanisation Trends in India’s Small Towns
item.description: The story so far: India continues to narrate its urban future through the loud vocabulary of megacities. But a quieter and far more consequential transformation is unfolding. Of India’s nearly 9,000 census and statutory towns, barely 500 qualify as large cities. The overwhelming majority are small towns, with populations below 1,00,000. This proliferation of small towns is a structural product of India’s capitalist development — and of its crisis.

item.title: Reassessing the Governor’s Address in India’s Legislative Framework
item.description: By digressing from the speech or walking out of the Assembly during the special address protocols, Tamil Nadu and Kerala Governors have shown disregard for the constitutional provisions and allegiance to the Centre.
